analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 21, 2026)
key_insights: Earnings are delivering the awaited boost to Tech, with APAC strength and NDX futures outperforming ahead of a catalyst-heavy day (NVDA GTC keynote, TSLA, META and IBM earnings).
US equities extended broadening on 10/20, with RTY outperforming NDX by more than 150bps. In Europe, politics hindered trade and rates pressure returned to focus.
A pick-up in US/Iran headline volatility drove large intraday moves in oil and rates relief. Markets faded the Middle East optimism quickly, and EU equities lagged despite de-escalation.

Catalysts for EU rotation and broadening to extend include rates and spreads finding a floor, earnings strength and a broader rotation into Quality. Domestic politics still drove EU equities on 10/20, with limited appetite to re-enter the trade.
EU earnings are the next focus, with strength widening beyond Tech and Energy. LSEG sees Q3 EU earnings growth of 20.7% YoY. A weaker EUR should add earnings support.

Key EU sectors to watch: Banks (a long-standing favourite that sold off on spread widening and is now testing the 200dma), Capital Goods on AI/data center demand (power generation and electrical equipment), and Staples (+11% MTD after a short squeeze and defensive rotation).

The Rates and Tech relationship is in focus this reporting season. Any slowdown in the capex narrative is expected to drive relief in global rates, as evidenced by the neocloud melt-up. Jay Barry attributed 10/20 long-end outperformance to KOSPI overnight weakness.

JPM views capital as the emerging key bottleneck in AI as financing risk grows. Credit strategists expect financing technicals, contingent liabilities and relative valuations to remain key drivers of spread performance, with dispersion persisting.

Memory market: the top three global memory shares are down 42% from the 2026 peak. JPM says the pricing reflects softer Frontier AI lab revenue run-rate trends, widening Neo-Cloud CDS spreads, tighter risk appetite and doubts about AI capex sustainability.
JPM calls the memory selloff perplexing because bottom-up supply/demand shows limited cracks: spot prices trending up, HBM ASP negotiations biased upward, and LTA order visibility extended.

UK labour market: payroll jobs show a tentative rise and the ILO unemployment rate dropped unexpectedly by a large amount. Vacancies are still falling and data reliability limits conclusions. Official data are converging toward JPM's nowcast of a soft but sustained employment recovery.
UK pay: there are tentative signs of firming in underlying AWE pay. BoE is on track for November, and a December move is unlikely barring stronger jobs and pay signals.

LatAm elections: the electoral dividend from pre-election fiscal largesse is fading. Security, geopolitics and anti-incumbency now dominate. Brazil's October 25 runoff is the last major test of the cycle, and Argentina's 2027 presidential election is next.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. Macro and thematics favor long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.

Broadening can return but more clearly in the US than the EU. EU earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but JPM needs stability in EGB spreads for conviction in EU broadening.

Longs: Tech and Supercycle themes (inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerables including application software), EU and JA Banks, EU Industrials, JA Machinery, GE Infra, EU Miners, EU Pharma, UKX, and selective Consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerables ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU Insurance, challenged industries (Autos, Chemicals, Asian Consumer Electronics, MedTech) and MDAX.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity on spending, pragmatism and ideology emerges, and short FR versus EU Domestics on politics and dislocation.

EM: since bottoming at end-July, EM has recovered over 9% of the drawdown but remains off YTD highs. JPM is bullish on global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, commodity broadening, policy easing scope and political catalysts, and favors country-relative trades.
EM trades: tactically long China Star 50 vs China Internet (KWEB), long Korea vs South East Asia (ASEA), and long Taiwan after the July Global Tech selloff. Hedges: long Brazil (EWZ) and EM (EEM).

JPM Positioning Intelligence: HF performance drawdown accelerated to -2.1% MTD globally (from -0.8% the prior week). Eq L/S -2.3% MTD, Quants -1% to -2%, Multi-Strats -2%, and APAC lagged most at -3.8% MTD.
Multi-Strat de-grossing was close to the worst of the past 2 years. US positioning was around the 40th percentile, while Europe was at the 11th and China/HK at the 8th.

Fragility came from crowded skews and high gross: AI Core Revenue positioning is at the 94th percentile (12m) and 99th (LT), Semis L/S is about 3.0x vs Software L/S about 1x, and Utilities HF positioning is near 10-year lows.

JPM sees echoes of 3Q23 more than 2018: US 10yr +82bps in 3Q26 vs +73bps in 3Q23, oil above +40% vs about +30%, and Quality outperforming Beta. HFs are about +6% YTD and equities up about 13% (MXWD) and 14% (SPX) YTD, which supports a likely 4Q rally barring fundamental deterioration.

tension_points.bull_case: EU earnings fundamentals are good (LSEG sees 20.7% YoY Q3 growth), positioning gives a buy signal, and a weaker EUR supports earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Domestic politics and EGB spread pressure keep investors from re-entering the trade, and EU lagged on 10/20 despite geopolitical de-escalation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of EGB spreads to stabilise, since JPM says it needs some stability in EGB spreads for broadening to gain conviction in EU.

tension_points.bull_case: Bottom-up supply/demand shows no crack: spot prices rising, HBM ASP negotiations biased upward, LTA order visibility extended.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares are pricing in softer Frontier AI lab revenue run-rate, widening Neo-Cloud CDS spreads, tighter risk appetite and doubts about AI capex sustainability.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong YTD cushion (HFs about +6%, SPX about +14%), a 2023-style setup and neutral US positioning favor stabilisation and a 4Q rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Crowded skews, high gross exposure and extreme AI/semis positioning could trigger further de-grossing, and the 2018 outcome remains possible.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in fundamentals (earnings or data), which would undercut the supportive YTD cushion.
